expectations.text: Asks the reader for exactly one thing (one question or one imperative request), not a list of things to try or report

That is a numbered list plus a follow-up question, more than exactly one request of the reader.

expectations.evidence: "Pull the trace or screenshot from a failed CI run and look at what's actually on the page when the timeout hits."

expectations.text: No dramatized tone ('Uh oh', 'Oh no', 'There seems to be a problem'); matter-of-fact

suggestions.assertion: Asks the reader for exactly one thing (one question or one imperative request), not a list of things to try or report
suggestions.reason: This run's "To find out which: 1. 2. 3." steps are sequential sub-parts of a single deliverable (view the artifact), similar in substance to run-3's prose-conditional path to the same deliverable, which passes. The verdict here turns on surface formatting (an explicit numbered list) rather than the number of substantively distinct asks, plus a genuinely separate closing question. Worth a wording tweak so graders aren't forced to weigh format over substance.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are otherwise sound; the one-ask assertion could specify more precisely how it treats an explicit numbered procedure that serves a single goal.
